about: The experiments chapter's narration for the two-year cut, round 5 and later (twin/video/experiments.py script(); TWIN_VIDEO_ROUND). It is narration_exp.json's script as a template: {path|format} puts in a number from out/twin<N>/video/experiments/facts.json and records it in the line's nums, so `python -m twin.video.experiments nums` checks it against the facts again; {path} puts in words the facts carry (say: each alloy described from its composition, small counts as words; footage: what out/footage holds for aluminium). nums lists the counts a line says as words: [the word, its path in facts.json, its format]. require names the conditions (experiments.CONDITIONS) the round's facts must meet for the line to be said: if one fails the build stops, so the line is reworded rather than spoken stale. if / unless choose between two wordings of one id. The lines as spoken for a round are written to out/twin<N>/video/experiments/narration/script.json.

lines.text: Each campaign is a function network: a chain of steps, where each step's results feed the next. BOFN, Bayesian optimization over function networks, models every step, not just the final score.
lines.src: experiments.Intro: the two networks (dag_anim's cards), then the pulse along each; BOFN: Astudillo and Frazier, 2021

lines.text: Here is each step itself, for one alloy from each campaign: the experiment, and the data it makes. Everything is simulated by the twin, unless a label says otherwise.
lines.src: experiments.Intro: the panel 'What follows' and 'How to read the labels'

lines.text: The aluminium alloy is design number {follow.flaime_al.design|d}: {say.al_describe}.
lines.src: exp_composition: the periodic table and the fractions (the committed event log of the replayed run; twin/spaces.py); the words come from the composition (exp_data.describe_al)

lines.text: On this map, it is one of {run.flaime_al.designs|d} designs in this run's log. The HPC stream's {hpc.flaime_al.evaluated_millions|.1f} million candidates are counted, not drawn.
lines.src: exp_composition: the card's title (the designs with a booking or a result in the log) and the tag under the map (the row's r5.hpc: candidates the stream evaluated for this campaign)

lines.text: The copper alloy is design number {follow.onr_cu.design|d}: {say.cu_describe}.
lines.src: exp_composition: copper's periodic table and fractions (the committed event log of the replayed run); the words come from the composition (exp_data.describe_cu)

lines.text: CALPHAD comes first. As the melt cools, a Scheil model follows how much of it has frozen. This curve is the one the optimizer sees.
lines.src: exp_scheil: the open-database node's curve drawn as the temperature falls (twin/thermo.py, the open parameter set)

lines.text: A full Scheil run on an open database adds the phases as they form. The twin's hidden truth differs again, as a real alloy would.
lines.src: exp_scheil: the pycalphad + scheil run with its phases, then the truth's curve (twin/thermo.py, the truth's parameter set)

lines.text: The twin's hidden truth differs from the node's curve, as a real alloy would.
lines.src: exp_scheil: the truth's curve beside the node's (no open database has this alloy's additions, so no independent run is drawn; said on screen)

lines.text: From its curve, the network takes two numbers: the liquidus, and a hot-cracking index.
lines.src: exp_scheil: the indicators drawn on the node's curve; the two read-outs highlighted (policies2.sim_of)

lines.text: Every run in {say.round_spoken} used this open node. The Thermo-Calc stand-in was never bought.
lines.src: exp_scheil: the line under the picture; facts.json sim_kinds: every simulation booked in the round's event logs is sim_open

lines.text: The twin stands in for the AM module with a moving point source of heat. It gives the melt pool's width and depth, and how fast the metal cools.
lines.src: exp_am: the laser track, the section, the point's thermal history (twin/physics.py rosenthal; truth_al.sim_am)

lines.text: This is not Thermo-Calc output, and no run bought this node. But the same model decides the porosity of every simulated build.
lines.src: exp_am: the statement on screen; facts.json sim_kinds; twin/truth_al.py build()

lines.text: For aluminium, the lab makes each alloy's powder itself. Then each alloy is printed, and every build is checked.
lines.src: exp_atomize, then exp_print (the old chapter's line at the powder node, reworded: before the in-house printer is online the first builds are printed at partners)

lines.text: {footage.line} The size distribution beside it is the twin's, for this alloy.
lines.src: exp_atomize: the lab's own aluminium run in the footage's frame (out/footage/manifest.json, subject al; exp_atomize.al_words says what is there) and the simulated laser-diffraction result

lines.text: Here, {say.atm_failed} of {say.atm_runs} runs failed, and {al.powder.cut_yield_pct|.0f} percent of the charge ended up in the printer's size range.
lines.src: exp_atomize: the mass balance (twin/instruments/atomize_yield.py on this lot)

lines.text: One build is {say.cubes} cubes, each at its own laser power and speed.
lines.src: exp_print: the plate with nine cubes growing, each labelled with its setting (twin/truth_al.py build on a 3 x 3 grid)

lines.text: Each cube's density and crack reading goes on the map. Too little energy leaves lack of fusion. Too much makes keyhole pores.
lines.src: exp_print: the power-speed map filling in; 'lack of fusion' and 'keyholing' where the twin's indices peak

lines.text: One build gives the network's print node {say.cubes} data points.
lines.src: exp_print: what the network takes (policies2.datasets, the print node: one row per cube)

lines.text: In the SEM, one electron beam scans the sample line by line, and four detectors each catch a different signal.
lines.src: exp_sem: the schematic of the column, the beam and the four detectors (illustrative), the four panels starting

lines.text: Secondary electrons show the powder's surface. Backscattered electrons show the section's pores and cracks. X-rays give the elements, and diffraction gives each grain's orientation.
lines.src: exp_sem: the four panels building from one raster position (twin/instruments/sem.py, eds.py, ebsd.py, full fidelity)

lines.text: Every image here is simulated by the twin, for this alloy.
lines.src: exp_sem: the tag on the data card and the third caption

lines.text: The network uses three of them: satellites on the powder, the section's pores and cracks, and the grain size. EDS only checks the composition.
lines.src: exp_sem: the four badges (policies2.powder_feat, campaign._soundness, policies2.section_out; EDS: measured, not an input)

lines.text: Bars are aged straight from the as-built state, then pulled. The furnace profile here is only illustrative: the twin models the strength it leaves.
lines.src: exp_mech: the direct-age profile, tagged illustrative (exp_data.heat_treatment: twin/truth_al.py strength models no profile; the test route books the furnace hours)

lines.text: The curve is the twin's simulated record of the test, up to fracture.
lines.src: exp_mech: the stress-strain curve drawn as the bar pulls (twin/instruments/tensile.py, full fidelity)

lines.text: Yield strength, {al.tensile.ys_MPa|.0f} megapascals, and elongation, {al.tensile.el_pct|.1f} percent, are the two numbers the network keeps.
lines.src: exp_mech: the read-outs (mean of three bars) and the two highlighted

lines.text: For copper, a one-hour corrosion screen ranks the DED deposits, and thirty days in seawater come before a utility is known.
lines.src: exp_corrosion (the old chapter's line, at the screen node)

lines.text: After an hour at rest, two quick scans give an early corrosion rate and a breakdown potential.
lines.src: exp_corrosion: the open-circuit potential over the hour, then the linear and cyclic scans and the two read-outs (twin/instruments/corrosion.py)

lines.text: In immersion, the coupon is weighed on days {cu.immersion.read_days.first|d}, {cu.immersion.read_days.second|d}, {cu.immersion.read_days.third|d} and {cu.immersion.read_days.fourth|d}. After any reading, the policy may stop it.
lines.src: exp_corrosion: mass loss against days as each interim reading arrives (Campaign._interim)

lines.text: On day {cu.immersion.days|d} it is cleaned and weighed: {cu.immersion.rate30_um_yr|.1f} micrometres a year.
lines.src: exp_corrosion: the day-30 point and the 30-day rate (measure_immersion, full fidelity)

lines.text: Both campaigns share one lab. From here on, each step is an icon that lights up while it runs.
lines.src: experiments.Outro: dag_anim's collapse to icons (the old chapter's line)
